title: A Ember for the Salt
premise: Wren Villalobos has spent his life hiding the beast-speaker gift that once bound his family to the mountain's old covenant, a pact broken generations ago when the crown betrayed the wild realms. When the king declares a hunt for all gifted, Wren flees into Thornfell and discovers the covenant's collapse is why the mountains are dying — and why the beasts are turning on humankind. To reforge it, he must carry an ember of the old pact to the Salt Court beneath the peaks, guided by a disgraced royal huntress who was ordered to kill him but chooses instead to defy her crown. At the Salt Court, Wren learns the ember demands a life freely given, and he offers his own; his sacrifice, witnessed by beast and human alike, reignites the covenant, restores his gift as a bridge rather than a secret, and forces the crown to recognize the wild realms or lose the mountains entirely.
about_author: Hazel Nystrom is the pen name of a former trail guide who spent six seasons in the northern ranges, mapping passes and collecting the folk-stories of isolated villages. She writes fantasy rooted in real wilderness, where the land itself is always a character with its own grievances.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Ear
chapters.summary: Wren Villalobos guides contraband through Thornfell using his hidden gift to bargain with wolves and ravens for safe passage. When a dying stag warns him that soldiers are asking about 'speakers' in the valley towns, he dismisses it — until he finds a neighbor's barn burned with a gifted child inside. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: dread settling over a carefully built double life.

chapters.title: Proclamation at Millbrook
chapters.summary: In town, Wren hears the crown's proclamation: all beast-speakers to be taken alive for questioning, dead if resistant. Royal huntress Sera Dain arrives leading the sweep, sharp-eyed and unsmiling. Wren's raven friend Kess is snared by a charm-net meant for speakers, forcing him to reveal his gift publicly to free her. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: the moment concealment becomes impossible.

chapters.title: Run Through the White Pass
chapters.summary: Hunted through a snowstorm, Wren uses every smuggler's road he knows while Sera tracks him with uncanny skill. Cornered at a cliff edge, she hesitates — because Kess shows her what Wren truly is, not the monster her orders describe. She lets him go and reports him dead. POV: alternating Wren and Sera. Emotional beat: the first crack in loyalty to the crown.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Remembers
chapters.summary: Sheltering in a ruined shrine, Wren touches the broken covenant stone and receives a vision of the original pact: his ancestors speaking for both realms, until a king demanded the beasts kneel. The stone gives him an ember of the old fire and a charge: carry it to the Salt Court before the last moon of winter. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: inheritance of a burden he never asked for.

chapters.title: The Huntress Returns
chapters.summary: Sera finds Wren again — sent back under suspicion after her report failed verification. Instead of arresting him, she offers a bargain: she'll guide him past the crown's cordon if he proves the covenant can be reforged, because her brother was taken in the first sweep. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: two enemies becoming reluctant allies out of shared grief.

chapters.title: Teeth in the Dark
chapters.summary: A beast-pack, maddened by the covenant's decay, ambushes them in the deep forest. Wren speaks with them rather than fights, learning their pain but also that some beasts now serve a shadow-thing feeding on the broken pact — and it knows about the ember. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: the cost of the gift made flesh; trust tested by violence.

chapters.title: The Crown's Long Arm
chapters.summary: Captured by a border patrol, the pair is dragged before the king's inquisitor, who reveals the crown broke the covenant deliberately to hoard the mountain's magic — and that Sera's brother is alive as leverage. Offered freedom for betrayal, each refuses in their own way and escapes during a beast-attack on the camp. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: choosing truth over safety, together.

chapters.title: Descent to the Salt Court
chapters.summary: Guided by Kess and the reconciled wolf-pack, they descend through drowned tunnels to the Salt Court, a cavern city of stone beasts grown silent since the breaking. The shadow-thing's servants pursue. Wren realizes the ember dims with every mile — time is nearly gone. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: awe curdling into desperation as hope runs thin.

chapters.title: The Ember Demands
chapters.summary: At the covenant's heart, the Salt Court's ancient voice names the price: a life freely given by one who carries both worlds. Sera offers herself; Wrefuses to let her. As the shadow-thing breaches the court, Wren steps into the flame, giving his gift, his name, his selfhood. POV: Wren, then Sera. Emotional beat: climax — sacrifice as the ultimate answer to power's corruption.

chapters.title: A Bridge Between Realms
chapters.summary: Wren does not die; the covenant remakes him as its living bridge, able to speak for both realms without belonging wholly to either. The shadow-thing dissolves, the beasts wake, and the crown — confronted by Sera's testimony and an awakened mountain — must treat or perish. Wren and Sera stand at the treeline, changed, beginning something new. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution — identity found not by hiding the gift, but by giving it away.
